titulo: Workshop kit for Horizonte and what changed in the market
lead: Time to put the pieces together. The final project is a 1-hour workshop kit for the support team at Horizonte Distribuidora, where Juliana works: diagnosis, script, exercises with answer key, incident mini-lesson, rubric, and follow-up. You rehearse, record 10 minutes, and evaluate yourself. At the end, you get the dashboard of what changed in the market in October 2026.
objetivo: deliver the complete 1-hour workshop kit for Horizonte's support team and give a recorded 10-minute lesson, evaluated with the rubric.

aprende.t: The 6 kit files and where each one was made

hero_alt: Workshop kit organized on a table: folder with script, exercise cards, scoring sheet and headset.

secoes.sub: Click each piece to see which lesson it comes from.

nos.detalhe: The questionnaire given (or simulated) to the support team, and the readout: how many at each level, active, curious and resistant, shadow AI.
The 5 parts with timing, the 5 principles marked, retrieval practice questions, backups and the block to skip.
Delegate, review and approve with support cases: a late-delivery complaint, a discount the customer asks for, an order hidden in the message. Each one with an answer key.
10 minutes on a real case tied to a Horizonte failure, with a rule and a test. Within the hour, use the 2-minute version.
4-level rubric (delegate, review, approve, apply) adapted to support, for the hands-on test at the end of the workshop.
Support champion with a backup, a weekly check-in of 15 to 20 minutes, and milestones at 30, 60 and 90 days with the before number.

secoes.legenda: A kit that exists only on paper is not ready yet: the 10-minute recording (step 2 below) shows what to change before the real class.

texto: Put the pieces from lessons 1 to 7 into one folder: diagnostico, roteiro, exercicios, incidente, rubrica, acompanhamento. Adapt everything to Horizonte's support work, using the vocabulary of the field.
Use only fictional lab data. No CPF or phone number, not even made-up ones that look real.

exemplo.texto: After this hour, the team answers complaints with AI, reviews with the 4 questions, and knows what only goes out with approval from someone with a name.

texto: Pick the hardest stretch: the opening with the fear named, or the review exercise. Record with your phone, speaking as you would to the class.
If you can, ask someone to play the skeptical participant, like Sérgio in lesson 3.

exemplo.texto: Time it. If the 10-minute stretch ran past 13, the 1-hour script won't fit.

texto: Watch the recording and score yourself on the 5 criteria in the checklist below, from 1 to 4. Note 1 thing to keep and 1 to change.
Ask AI for a second opinion with the ready-made prompt. It doesn't decide for you: it points out what you may be overlooking.

exemplo.texto: Keep: the discount case. Change: I waited only 4 seconds after the question.

texto: Fix the script with what the recording showed and complete the kit checklist.
In real life, show the kit to the client (here, Carlos, the owner, with Juliana) before the workshop and agree on the number that will be measured in 30 days.

exemplo.texto: Folder with 6 files + link to the 10-minute video + completed checklist.

secoes.sub: The checklist closes the kit; the prompt gives the second opinion.

blocos.conteudo:
KIT CHECKLIST · 1-hour workshop · customer service · Horizonte Distribuidora

PARTS
[ ] Diagnostic: questionnaire + reading (levels, groups, shadow AI)
[ ] 1-hour script in 5 parts, adding up to 60 min, with a buffer and a block to skip
[ ] The 5 principles marked in the script
[ ] 3 exercises (delegate, review, approve) with answer key, customer service cases
[ ] Incident mini-lesson (2-minute version inside the hour) with date and source
[ ] 4-level rubric adapted to customer service
[ ] Follow-up plan: champion + backup, weekly check-in, 30/60/90
[ ] Today's number agreed on to measure in 30 days
[ ] Fictional data only; no promise of jobs or guaranteed results

AI TRAINER RUBRIC (10-min recording · 1 to 4 each)
1. Why: did you open with the class's problem, with a number?   ___
2. Practice: does the class do more than watch?                  ___
3. Retrieval: did you ask and wait ~15 s?                       ___
4. Safety: risk with a real case, without alarmism?             ___
5. Landing: commitment with a date and a follow-up scheduled?   ___
Keep: <...>   Change: <...>

secoes.sub: The kit is the deliverable of this program.

exercicios.texto: Build the folder for the 1-hour workshop kit for the Horizonte Distribuidora customer service team (Juliana), using the lab as the scenario.
exercicios.pronto: all the PARTS lines of the checklist are checked and the 6 files are in the folder.

exercicios.texto: Record a 10-minute segment of the workshop, grade it with the AI trainer rubric, and ask for the second opinion with the prompt. Adjust the script.
exercicios.pronto: the video exists, the 5 criteria have scores, there is 1 item to keep and 1 to change, and the script has a version 2 with the change made.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Why record 10 minutes before giving the workshop?
opcoes: Because the recording shows what the script on paper hides: timing, silence, and tone
Because the certification requires a long video
perguntas.explica: On paper, everything fits. Recorded, you see that you waited 4 seconds, that the case took 6 minutes, or that the tone scared people.

perguntas.p: The kit is ready, but no one agreed on today's number. What is missing?
opcoes: Nothing, the number is found out later
The baseline: without it, on day 90 there is no result to show
perguntas.explica: Without a before number, no one knows whether the training helped. It's the same flaw as the Horizonte dashboard (F11).

perguntas.p: What is the second-opinion prompt for?
opcoes: For the AI to rewrite the whole kit
To point out weak spots, risks, and what you might be overlooking; you decide
perguntas.explica: A second opinion clarifies, it doesn't decide. The prompt asks it not to rewrite and to point out promises you can't keep.

perguntas.p: The "What changed" panel gets outdated. What do you do with lessons 1 to 7?
opcoes: Redo all of them every quarter
Keep them: the method doesn't change; you only swap the panel
perguntas.explica: The method (teaching adults, workshop, cycle, rubric) survives a change of tool. The panel is what changes every quarter.

itens.texto: Why, real problem, practice, retrieval, and next week.
Diagnostic, 5 parts, delegate-review-approve cycle adapted to the area.
A real case without alarmism, a 4-level rubric, a champion, and 90 days.
Kit tested on video; the market dashboard is updated every quarter.

secoes.sub: Dashboard updated every quarter. The method in lessons 1 to 7 stays; the facts below change.
paragrafos: AI literacy required in the EU (since 02/02/2025). Article 4 of the AI Act requires AI literacy measures for people who use AI at work. It is the most direct argument for selling training. Article 4.
High risk postponed to 02/12/2027 (agreement of 05/07/2026). The Omnibus package postponed the high-risk rules in Annex III; AI literacy still applies. Gibson Dunn.

Agents that deliver finished work (07/09/2026). ChatGPT Work produces documents, spreadsheets, and slides, and works for hours. That is why lesson 4 trains you to delegate, review and approve, not to write prompts. ChannelLife.
Exposed AI-built apps (May/2026). About 380 thousand public apps were scanned, and close to 5 thousand held sensitive company data. A ready-made case for lesson 6. HKU.

Agent that acted without authorization (10/09/2026). Anthropic reported models acting on real websites during evaluations, including submitting forms, and cut off live internet access in those tests. ResultSense.

Grok deepfakes under investigation (01/26/2026). The European Commission opened a formal investigation into X under the Digital Services Act. A case for talking about images of real people and voice scams. Al Jazeera.
Brazil: governance trailing adoption (Sep/2026). Only 27% of Brazilian companies say they have mature AI governance, according to Deloitte. Training the team is the first step. Deloitte.
